overview: East of the Great Wall of Aenor, on the same landmass as the Middle Lands, lie the Magical Lands: the snow ridges of the Magic Mountains, the Herrodon rim against the Kusmeel, the largest and oldest forest in Aoaz, a belt of giant fungi along the long rift sea, and Dragon Mountain, from which the dragons come. The elves here were never conquered, not by Volgan's corrupted kin in the First Age and not by Elzon in the Third, and they sent no army to save the men of Aenor after Edran's folly in the Ember Lands. In 4A 1748 they live in seven small realms scattered where their histories put them: the elected houses of the Magical Forest, a hill queen on the northern rim, a federation of lake groves bound to Lerendor, pass-wardens in the southern crags, the elder houses of the Long Shore, the loremasters of the Archive and a few thousand keepers of the dragon roosts. Men live here too, in the refugees' vale of Teste, the mixed port at the Rift Narrows and the pilgrim valleys of the Worshipdom, and the mycids keep the fungal belt to themselves. The years in this data are the continuous count from Aen's victory that every regional history shares: a First Age year is itself, a Second Age year adds 1,675, a Third Age year adds 3,808 (taking the proposed Third Age of 1,260 years) and a Fourth Age year adds 5,068, so that 4A 1748 is year 6,816; a realm or place older than the numbered years carries 0, and every dated entry also gives its date as the world writes it, in the form 4A 1748. Everything not marked established is a proposal under the owner's decision L1.

ages.name: The Age of Kingdoms
ages.summary: Before Aen the elves already held the Magical Lands and the dragons already nested on Dragon Mountain, and the elves alone could ask them for help. The rift-coast elves traded with men of the East across the rift for longer than any chronicle, and the hill elves lived on both sides of the range; no people of men had yet settled east of it. Long before Aen the eastern coast of the elven woods and the East were one land, and the road of the Bridge Kingdom crossed the elven shore under a treaty of passage; the elves were its neighbours, never its subjects.

ages.name: The First Age
ages.summary: To Aen's kingdom the elves were courteous strangers beyond the range. When Volgan came, corrupted elves and dragons fought in his armies, the pass-wardens of Nolorim swore to hold the heights above Mirolon, and the elves of the Magical Forest joined Edran's Grand Alliance under their war-speaker; many of them died afterwards in the Ember Lands campaign they had warned against.

ages.name: The Second Age
ages.summary: The age of the elves' distrust: the hill houses of the west were called home over the range, the Archive was founded to keep the names of the fallen, and healers still crossed to help men while the realms refused every summons to war. In 2A 2121 the Refusal was voted, and when Elzon took Aenor no elven army came.

ages.name: The Third Age
ages.summary: The Order never conquered the Magical Lands. The elves held its hosts at the passes, sheltered the Vale's refugees and let some of them settle the Teste Vale, cut down their own northern wood to sever the Black Roots, and held their magical places through the War of Unbinding without reforming the Grand Alliance; the length of 1,260 years is proposed.

countries.name: Magical Forest

founding.story: The council elves say the Living Forest was sung before it grew, and that their houses met beneath its oldest Singing Grove to listen before any of them thought to speak; they keep many stories of how their kind began and hold none of them to be fact. No people of men remembers a time when the forest was not theirs, and it is the oldest realm in Aoaz that has never been conquered, not by Volgan's corrupted kin and not by the Great Necromancer.

roots.story: Long before Aen the houses that became the council came into the Living Forest from many directions, and their own songs disagree about whence; what every song agrees on is the quarrel. Each house claimed the glades it had found first, and for a long season the forest knew feuds over hunting runs and springs. The houses met under the oldest Singing Grove meaning to fight, and by their own telling they stayed to listen, because the grove was singing. The first precedent was made there: a house that wished to speak had first to pick up a bough the grove had let fall, hold it while it spoke and lay it down for the next, and nobody might break a bough from a living tree to get a turn. From that night come the customs that still shape the realm: the council's vote and its book of precedents; the rule that the houses take fallen wood only and never cut a living tree, which they wrote even into the Worshipdom's grant of the Zilin valleys; and the Speaking Bough itself, a fallen bough kept in the council-hall at Lyrion and passed from hand to hand at every Elder Moot. The rule was broken once, in 3A 802, when the houses felled the northern wood themselves to cut the Black Roots' anchors; each house carried one bough of the trees it had felled to Lyrion, and the heap lies behind the council-hall as the hardest page of the book, written in wood. In 4A 1748 a First Speaker still takes office by picking the bough up from the floor rather than being handed it, and a house that interrupts a speaker who holds it loses its voice for the session.

sign.device: A fallen bough laid level across the field, leafed at one end, in mist grey on deep wood green: the Speaking Bough of the council-hall.
sign.origin: The bough on the council's banners is the Speaking Bough, the fallen branch the first houses picked up under the oldest Singing Grove so that only one of them would speak at a time. The war-speaker Sirael carried a bough of the same grove at Dardan instead of a standard, and the companies of the Grand Alliance learned to look for it in the smoke; after the Ember Lands the houses sewed it on grey-green cloth so that every company of the forest would carry the precedent with it. It is always shown lying level, never upright and never held, because no house owns it.
sign.meaning: That the right to speak is lent and laid down again, and that the forest takes only what it gives: to its own houses a promise of the council's peace, and to anyone who would cut the living wood a warning.

dynasties.name: The First Speakers of the Houses
dynasties.notable: The houses of the Magical Forest vote, keep a book of precedents and choose a First Speaker, who may hold the office for as long as the houses trust her; no house has a right to it. Lusiel of the house of Velakorin is First Speaker in 4A 1748, and Sirael, the war-speaker of the Grand Alliance, was of the same house.

events.name: The First Listening
events.summary: Feuding houses meet under the oldest Singing Grove meaning to fight and stay to listen; the first precedent is made there, that a house speaks only while it holds a bough the grove has let fall.

events.name: The War-Speaker at Dardan
events.summary: The houses choose Sirael war-speaker for the Grand Alliance, wary of the human crown but warier of Volgan; she fights at Dardan beside the host of King Lorien, and her name is the first in the forest's book of the fallen.

events.name: The Ember Lands Losses
events.summary: The forest's companies follow Edran into the Ember Lands against Sirael's warning, and many of them do not come back; the book of precedents records the campaign as the reason the houses will not again send an army at a king's request.

events.name: The Refusal
events.summary: When the crown of Aenor summons the elven kingdoms against Elzon's war, the houses vote to send no army, remembering the Ember Lands; healers and individual travellers still go west, and the Refusal is written into the book as a precedent every realm of the Kindred keeps.

events.name: The Fallen Forest
events.summary: When the Black Roots reach the northern wood, the elves cut the trees themselves to sever the Necromancer's anchors in the ground; the felled wood still lies where it fell, and nobody has lived in the Fallen Forest since.

events.name: The Boughs of the Felled Wood
events.summary: Each house carries one bough of the northern trees it felled against the Black Roots to Lyrion, and the heap behind the council-hall becomes the one page of the book of precedents that is written in wood.

events.name: The Accord of the Passes
events.summary: The houses agree with the restored crown to keep the eastern forts of the Kingson Pass while men keep the western, and the tolls are taken at Kingson.

events.name: The Pilgrim Valleys
events.summary: The houses grant the three Zilin valleys south of the forest to the hermitage of the Deliverer as pilgrim ground, on condition that no pilgrim cuts a living tree; the grant is renewed every seventh year.

events.name: The Long Winter
events.summary: When Kingson doubles the toll on elven silver, the houses close the eastern fort of the Kingson Pass for a winter; the Kingson Reckoning of 4A 1690 halves the toll again and the fort reopens.

events.name: The Shore Debate
events.summary: In the Elder Moot the houses of Lccimio propose to set the Refusal aside in return for a treaty of peace with the eastern courts; the First Speaker's houses refuse, and the shore remembers it.

rivalries.nature: Partners at the Kingson Pass and quarrellers over its tolls since the Long Winter of 4A 1689.
The delving-clans of the range keep elves off their roads under the Iron Charter, and the houses do not ask to use them.
Kin of the Kindred divided by the Question of the Refusal since the Shore Debate of 4A 1702.

countries.capitalReason: Lyrion grew round the oldest Singing Grove of the Living Forest, where the houses first met to listen; a council that keeps a book of precedents meets where the first precedent was set.
countries.today: The Magical Forest in 4A 1748 is an elected council of houses under First Speaker Lusiel Velakorin, some 180,000 elves with a few mycid families on the Elwen, the largest and oldest realm of the elves and the keeper of the Refusal. It is at peace with everyone, can call an Elder Moot of the Kindred, and with the other elven realms can ask the dragons of Dragon Mountain for help that no crown of men can command.

divergence.what: The houses vote to set the Refusal aside and march when the dark comes west.
divergence.consequence: An elven host fights beside men for the first time since the Ember Lands, the Kindred divides over the vote, and the book of precedents gains its hardest page.

divergence.what: The houses refuse to entrust a dragon to the heir who comes east looking for help.
divergence.consequence: He returns to the Middle Lands on foot, late, and without the wizard and his servant beside him; the war's turn waits on whoever can reach him.

divergence.what: The houses close the passes and hide the woods for the length of the war.
divergence.consequence: The Magical Lands keep out of the war of men entirely, the eastern host finds the forest's edges empty, and Aenor fights alone.

divergence.what: In the debate over the Refusal a speaker breaks a bough from a living tree to speak out of turn.
divergence.consequence: The council splits over the broken precedent, the houses that walk out of Lyrion hold a moot of their own, and the Kindred must decide which bough it follows.

countries.name: Herrodon

founding.story: The hill elves of the northern rim keep a hall on the south slope of the Herrodon Mountains whose first queen, they say, was acclaimed there by the houses of the hills before the sea had a name; the hall's book begins with her and no year. Herrodon has always been a queenship of the hall, never of blood alone, and the hill elves were once spread on both sides of the Great Wall of Aenor until the Second Age called them home.

roots.story: Long before Aen the hill elves lived on both faces of the range that men later called the Great Wall of Aenor, moving with the snowline as the years turned, and they had houses but no hall. Their realm was made by a winter they still call the White Winter, when the snow came down off the Herrodon rim in one night and buried the summer camps of the south slope. A keeper of the herds, whom the hall's book names only as the First Queen, was lost on the rim in the storm and followed a white owl down to a hollow under the crags where the wind could not reach; she kept a fire alive there, went back into the snow again and again, and by spring she had brought most of the houses into the hollow. The houses acclaimed her in the hollow that became the hall of Verozo, gave her its key, and swore that no house of the hills would ever again be left out in the snow. From that oath come the queenship by acclamation rather than by blood, the queen's duty to bring home anyone who is lost, the summons home of 2A 3, the seat kept empty for the lost household of the Kingdom Forests, and Herrodon's protection of the refugee families of Teste. The hall still keeps owls in its roof-beams, no hill elf will harm one, and a queen lays the hall-key down only when she can no longer go out into the snow herself.

sign.device: A white owl with its wings raised, facing out, on night slate: the Hall-Owl of Verozo.
sign.origin: The owl is the bird that led the First Queen down from the rim to the hollow that became the hall, and an owl has roosted in the hall's roof-beam for as long as the hall's book runs. The queens' wardens first carried it into the snow as a banner of search, sewn white on dark cloth so that the lost could see it against the slope at dusk, and the hill houses who answered the summons home of 2A 3 walked back over the range behind it. It goes out whenever the queen sends for someone, and it hangs over the empty seat of the lost household.
sign.meaning: That no one of the hills is left out in the snow: to the hill houses and the men of Teste a promise of shelter and of being sought, and to the lost household of the west an invitation that does not lapse.

dynasties.name: The Queens of the Hall of Verozo
dynasties.notable: A queen is acclaimed in her hall by the hall-keepers of the hill houses and reigns until she lays the hall-key down; daughters of queens have been acclaimed and passed over in roughly equal number. Herrowyn is queen in 4A 1748.

events.name: The White Winter
events.summary: The snow comes off the Herrodon rim in one night and buries the summer camps; a herd-keeper follows an owl to a hollow under the crags, brings the houses into it and is acclaimed there as the First Queen.

events.name: The Boundary Groves
events.summary: A flood moves the Andos Water's channel, and the Boundary Groves that both realms tended now stand on Andos Enda's bank; Herrodon's queen will not give up her houses' rites there, and the oldest feud of the Kindred begins.

events.name: The Summons Home
events.summary: After the Ember Lands campaign the queen calls the hill houses of the western woods home over the range; one household refuses and stays in the Kingdom Forests, and the queen writes its name in her hall's book as lost.

events.name: The Vale Under the Rim
events.summary: Refugees from the Vale who have come over the Kingson Pass settle the empty Teste Vale under the rim, and the queen takes them under her protection on condition that they feed her hall; Teste has kept the bargain since.

events.name: The Envoys to the West
events.summary: Queen Herrowyn's mother sends envoys to the lost household in the Kingdom Forests to ask it home a second time; they come back with gifts and no answer, and the queen's hall still keeps a seat empty for its Eldest.

rivalries.nature: The Boundary Groves feud since 1A 744: never fought with arms, always fought with rites, embassies and silence.
The lost kin of the west, whom the queens have asked home twice and will ask again.

countries.capitalReason: Verozo stands on the lower slope of the Herrodon Mountains above the Teste Vale, where the hall can see the vale that feeds it and the rim that shelters it, and where the first queen was acclaimed.
countries.today: Herrodon in 4A 1748 is a hill queenship of some 55,000 elves under Queen Herrowyn, with the men of the Teste Vale under its protection. It keeps the Boundary Groves feud with Andos Enda alive by ceremony, remembers the lost kin of the west, and its queen has said she would set the Refusal aside if the dragons were ever threatened.

divergence.what: The queen sets the Refusal aside when the eastern host threatens the dragons' mountain.
divergence.consequence: The hill elves march before the Magical Forest votes, the Kindred must follow or disown them, and the Boundary Groves feud is forgotten in a season.

divergence.what: Herrodon and Andos Enda settle the Boundary Groves before the war.
divergence.consequence: The two oldest rivals of the Kindred stand together, and the lake groves bring Lerendor's letters to a queen who can answer them.

divergence.what: The lost household of the Kingdom Forests answers the third summons and comes home over the range.
divergence.consequence: The empty seat in Verozo is filled, Dunelaeth's western woods are left to men, and Herrodon gains a household that has lived beside Aenor's realms for an age and knows their courts.

countries.name: Andos Enda

founding.story: The lake elves of the Andos Water name their houses after the waters they live on and move the name when they move, so for most of their history there was no realm, only groves. In the year the Aenoran chroniclers give, the groves of the Andos lakes swore the Weir Compact to share the water and judge their quarrels at a Water-Court, and the federation took its name from the water that bound it.

roots.story: Long before Aen the lake elves were boat-folk with no land of their own: groves that lived on the waters of the Andos, took the water's name and moved the name with them when the water changed. Their oldest custom is the guest-night, in which a lake house shelters any stranger for one night and sends him on at dawn, because a boat can carry a guest but cannot keep one. The federation was forced on them by a drought. In the Year of the Broken Weirs, a few years before the Weir Compact, the lakes fell so low that the groves broke one another's weirs to keep their own water, and a boat carrying the children of the grove of Ilawen was overturned in the race loosed by a broken dam. The elder of that grove, Enlire, called the groves to the largest lake and would not let them ashore; she held the first Water-Court in her own boat, moored on open water, so that no grove could claim the ground the court stood on. The Weir Compact of 1A 480 was sworn there, and the court has sat afloat ever since. From that drought come the Water-Court's law of weirs and boats, the rule that the Speaker owns no land and takes the name of the largest lake, the federation's habit of judging by water rather than by blood, and its old fear of every dry summer. Its boats still carry Lerendor's letters and the guests of every realm, and they still put them ashore at dawn.

sign.device: A slender lake-boat with a tall curled prow, seen from the side and empty, in water silver on lake teal: the Court-Boat of Enliras.
sign.origin: The boat is the Court-Boat, in which Enlire held the first Water-Court on open water so that no grove could own the ground the court sat on. It is the same boat, rebuilt plank by plank whenever a plank fails, that is moored on the largest lake at Enliras today, and the Speaker sits in it to judge. The groves sewed it on their sails when the Weir Compact was sworn in 1A 480, and they show it empty because the court belongs to no grove and any grove may come aboard.
sign.meaning: That the water is shared and judged in common: to the groves the promise of a fair court afloat, and to strangers the lake elves' welcome, which takes them in at dusk and carries them on at dawn.

dynasties.name: The Speakers of the Water-Court
dynasties.notable: The groves choose a Speaker to sit over the Water-Court and speak for the federation abroad; the Speaker takes the name of the largest lake for the length of office. Andosiel is Speaker in 4A 1748.

events.name: The Year of the Broken Weirs
events.summary: A drought drops the Andos lakes, the groves break one another's weirs, and the children of the grove of Ilawen drown in a loosed race; Enlire calls the groves onto open water and holds the first court in her boat.

events.name: The Weir Compact
events.summary: The lake groves swear to share the weirs and the boats of the Andos Water and to bring every quarrel to the Water-Court at Enliras.

events.name: The Boundary Groves
events.summary: A flood moves the Andos Water's channel and leaves the Boundary Groves on the federation's bank; the groves claim them, Herrodon will not give up its rites there, and the feud begins.

events.name: Sent On at Dawn
events.summary: Families fleeing the Vale come over the Kingson Pass to the lakes; the groves shelter them for a night and send them on at dawn, as the lake elves send every guest, and some of them settle the empty Teste Vale.

events.name: The Harbour Accord of Enliras
events.summary: After a century of letters between Enliras and Sonargur, the federation grants Leren ships harbour on the Andos Water but declines the Leren Compact itself, for the groves still remember the Elven Refusal and will not bind themselves to a crown of men.

rivalries.nature: The Boundary Groves feud since 1A 744, kept alive by ceremony rather than war.

countries.capitalReason: Enliras is the water-garden on the largest lake of the Andos Water, where the Water-Court sits because every grove can reach it by boat in a day.
countries.today: Andos Enda in 4A 1748 is a federation of lake groves of some 50,000 elves under Speaker Andosiel, courted by Lerendor, whose Leren Compact it has so far declined, and bound to Herrodon by an old quarrel. Its boats carry the letters between Sonargur and the elven realms, and its Water-Court judges weirs, boats and the Boundary Groves.

divergence.what: If Lerendor wins the federation into the Leren Compact, Sonargur can call on it when Lerendor leaves the Treaty of the Narrow Strait.
divergence.consequence: The lake elves must choose between a crown of men and the Refusal, and the Kindred learns whether a compact of letters weighs more than a book of precedents.

divergence.what: The groves shelter the refugees of the eastern invasion for longer than one night.
divergence.consequence: The lake elves break their own oldest custom, the Andos Water fills with strangers, and the federation becomes the Magical Lands' refuge.

divergence.what: In a hard drought a Speaker brings the Water-Court ashore and claims the lake ground for the federation.
divergence.consequence: The groves gain a seat and lose their oldest law, and Herrodon reads the claim as a claim on the Boundary Groves.

countries.name: Nolorim

founding.story: When Volgan fell on Mirolon, the elven families of the southern crags saw his fires from the Nolorim East Pass above the Lake of Mirolon and swore, each family to one post, that nothing of his would come up through the heights into the Magical Lands. They kept the oath, and the families who swore it have kept their posts ever since as the Nolorim wardenship.

roots.story: Before they were wardens the families of the southern crags were herders of the heights, few and proud, who drove their goats over the passes above the Lake of Mirolon and traded milk and wool with the men of Mirolon's shore, whom they counted as neighbours. When Volgan fell on Mirolon in 1A 1150, the herders saw his fires come round the lake by night and could not reach the shore in time. Their eldest herder, Nolanwe, blew the great horn of the heights to warn the lake towns and blew it until its bell split, and the warning still came too late; at dawn the families saw what was left of the shore. They swore that same morning, each family to one post, that nothing of Volgan's would come up through the heights and that the warning would never again come late, and the cracked horn was hung in the first warden-hall, where every Pass-Warden since has sworn on it. From that night comes the whole law of the wardenship: one family to one post, a vigil that never stops, a count of everyone who crosses, a Pass-Warden unmade if a vigil breaks on his watch, the watch on the Lake of Mirolon that has never once ceased, and an old shame that keeps the wardens closer to Mirolon's people than most elves are to any men. In 4A 1748 the post-captains still learn the horn-calls before they learn the bow, and a warden who sends word late is not forgiven.

sign.device: A curved war-horn with a split bell, mouth to the left, in dawn silver on pass grey-green: the Cracked Horn of Ennaton.
sign.origin: The horn is the herders' great horn that Nolanwe blew over the Lake of Mirolon on the night Volgan's fires came round the shore, until its bell split. The families who swore the Oath of the Posts at dawn sewed it on the cloth of the first watch-post, and the horn itself has hung over the warden-hall at Ennaton since the hall was built. The wardens show it cracked on purpose, so that every post-captain who looks up at it remembers that a warning once came too late.
sign.meaning: That the warning will always come in time: to Mirolon and the lake shore the promise of an unsleeping watch, and to anything coming up from the south a threat that the heights already know it is coming.

dynasties.name: The Pass-Wardens of the Posts
dynasties.notable: The post-captains of the warden families elect a Pass-Warden, who holds the office until a vigil is broken on his watch; no Pass-Warden has ever been unmade that way. Nolwe is Pass-Warden in 4A 1748.

events.name: The Oath of the Posts
events.summary: As Mirolon falls to Volgan, the families of the crags swear to hold the Nolorim passes post by post, and the first Pass-Warden lights the watch-fire on the East Pass.

events.name: The Cracked Horn
events.summary: Nolanwe blows the herders' great horn over the Lake of Mirolon until its bell splits, the warning comes too late for the shore, and the families swear on the cracked horn at dawn.

events.name: The Heights Held
events.summary: The Order's hosts try the Nolorim West Pass from the Herez road three times in a century and never cross it; the wardens leave the cairns of the Order's dead on the pass road as a warning.

events.name: The South Pass Tower
events.summary: Under the Accord of the Passes the wardens take the eastern tower of the South Pass, facing the Klungori Guard's tower across the saddle.

events.name: The Pilgrim Road
events.summary: The wardens let the Deliverer's pilgrims cross the South Pass to the Zilin Hills unarmed and in daylight, and count every one of them.

rivalries.nature: The wardenship was sworn against the realm beyond the south, and its post-captains still watch the Lake of Mirolon every night.

countries.capitalReason: Ennaton, the wardens' hall, stands on the West Pass above the Herez road, at the post the Order tried hardest to take, because the Pass-Warden keeps his hall where the vigil is most likely to break.
countries.today: Nolorim in 4A 1748 is a pass-wardenship of some 15,000 elves under Pass-Warden Nolwe, holding the Nolorim Heights and the eastern tower of the South Pass. Its families count every pilgrim, merchant and stranger who crosses, and its watch on the Lake of Mirolon is the only one in the Magical Lands that never stopped.

divergence.what: The wardens see the fires of the south in time and send their count to Mirolon and to Herez.
divergence.consequence: Mirolon has a season's warning and Herez an extra garrison, and the hosts of the south find every pass above the lake held.

divergence.what: A post falls in the war and the Pass-Warden is unmade for the first time.
divergence.consequence: The heights open to the south, the wardens elect a new Pass-Warden in the field, and the Magical Lands lose the one watch they relied on.

divergence.what: A Pass-Warden has the Cracked Horn mended and declares the old shame paid.
divergence.consequence: The wardens turn from Mirolon toward the Kindred, the lake shore loses its most faithful watchers, and the post-captains who refuse the mending keep a vigil of their own.

countries.name: Lccimio

founding.story: The rift-coast elves of the northern shore had traded with men of the East for longer than any chronicle, and their names had long carried foreign sounds; in the plague centuries, when eastern ships brought fever as well as silver, the elder houses of the shore met at Hidirim and bound themselves under one quay-book, so that a ship turned away from one harbour could not be taken in at the next. The Long Shore has kept the quay-book and its council of elder houses ever since.

roots.story: Long before Aen the rift-coast elves of the northern shore lived beside a people of men they could reach on foot, for the East was not yet cut off from the Magical Lands, and their oldest rolls name eastern families who were their friends over many lifetimes of men. Among those friends a custom grew up: an elven house that kept a friendship with an eastern family took one of that family's names as a guest-name, and the eastern family gave the house seed of its orchards in return. When the neck of land broke and the sea came in between the shores, the friends were left on the far side; the shore-houses kept their guest-names and kept the seed in sealed jars as a pledge that the friendship would be taken up again. The foreign sounds in Lccimio's names come from those guest-names, the shore's patient dealing with the East comes from that pledge, and the quay-book of 2A 300, sworn when eastern ships brought fever as well as silver, comes from the same reckoning that a friendship is kept by rules and not by trust alone. The jars were opened at last in 4A 610, when the houses planted the orchards of the northern shore in the fields the Necromancer's age had left empty, and the oldest trees of Hidirim are said to grow from that seed. In 4A 1748 the houses would trade the Refusal for an eastern peace because they have waited for one longer than any realm of men has stood, and every new Elder plants a tree of the old seed-line in the quay-garden of Hidirim.

sign.device: A round-headed fruit tree in white blossom, standing alone, in quay silver on rift teal: the Pledge-Tree of Hidirim.
sign.origin: The tree is the Pledge-Tree, grown from the seed the eastern friends of the shore-houses gave them across the neck before the land broke, kept in sealed jars through the ages and planted at Hidirim in 4A 610. The shore's banner of the plague centuries showed the sealed jar, and when the jar was opened the houses sewed the tree in its place; the elder houses carried it into the Elder Moot at the Shore Debate of 4A 1702. It is always shown in blossom and never in fruit, because the pledge is not yet kept.
sign.meaning: That an old friendship with the East is still owed: to the eastern courts an offer of peace and trade, and to the Kindred a reminder that the Long Shore was a friend of men across the water before it sat in any moot.

dynasties.name: The Elder Houses of the Long Shore
dynasties.notable: The heads of the elder houses sit as the council and choose an Elder to keep the quay-book; the office passes among the houses of the orchards and the houses of the quays in turn. Lusmio is Elder in 4A 1748.

events.name: Neighbours Across the Shore
events.summary: The oldest rolls of the rift-coast elves name eastern neighbours who could be reached on foot, and some of Lccimio's family names still carry their sounds.

events.name: The Seed Pledge
events.summary: When the neck breaks and the sea parts the shores, the shore-houses seal the seed their eastern friends gave them in jars and keep their guest-names as a pledge that the friendship will be taken up again.

events.name: The Quay-Book
events.summary: The elder houses bind the shore's harbours under one law of ships, tolls and quarantine, and the quay-book becomes the oldest written law on the rift.

events.name: The Port at the Narrows
events.summary: The houses of the rift coast grant a charter to the Alerhic quay-houses at the Rift Narrows, and Luv-zhise becomes the crossing to the East under elven law.

events.name: The Orchards Planted
events.summary: The houses plant the orchards of the northern shore in the fields the Necromancer's age left empty, and Lccimio's fruit and wine reach Parim by the Kingson Pass for the first time.

events.name: The Shore Debate
events.summary: In the Elder Moot the houses propose to set the Refusal aside in return for peace with the eastern courts; the Magical Forest refuses, and the shore has grumbled about it since.

rivalries.nature: Divided over the Question of the Refusal since the Shore Debate of 4A 1702.

countries.capitalReason: Hidirim is the best harbour of the northern rift shore, where the elder houses first met to bind the quays, and the quay-book is kept there because it is the harbour every eastern ship tries first.
countries.today: Lccimio in 4A 1748 is a council of elder houses of some 60,000 rift-coast elves under Elder Lusmio, holding the northern rift shore from Mushroom Head to the Gorlab Sea with its orchards and quays. Its houses know the eastern courts better than any elves alive, would trade the Refusal for an eastern peace, and lie first in the path of anyone who crosses the rift from the East.

divergence.what: When the eastern host crosses the rift, the elder houses make their own peace with it.
divergence.consequence: The northern shore is spared and the Kindred divided, the host's road into the Magical Lands lies open, and the Magical Forest must choose between its book and its kin.

divergence.what: The houses close the quays and fight at the Rift Narrows with Luv-zhise.
divergence.consequence: The eastern host is held at the water for a season, and the Long Shore pays for it with its orchards.

divergence.what: An eastern court sends an envoy who can recite the guest-names of the shore-houses.
divergence.consequence: The Long Shore takes up the oldest friendship of the rift, opens its quays to the East and makes a peace of its own that the Kindred never voted.

countries.name: Eldafaen

founding.story: After the Ember Lands campaign a house of loremasters on the southern rift shore gathered the names, letters and songs of the elves who had died in the Alliance's wars, so that no one would ever again ask the elves to march without reading them first. The house became the Archive at the end of the old roads, and it has kept everything the Kindred has written since, and a great deal that others have written about the Kindred.

roots.story: The loremasters keep a treaty older than their house: long before Aen the elders of the shore let the road of an eastern kingdom cross the southern rift shore on condition that no army of that kingdom came with it, and the house that kept the treaty kept the road's end at Lenkei, where the old roads still stop. It was a house of witnesses, whose duty was to see who came along the road and to remember it. Its great change came after the Ember Lands. When the companies of the Grand Alliance came home along the old roads, those who carried the spears of the fallen laid them down at the road's end, and the witnesses would not let the companies pass until every spear had been named. They broke each spear across the treaty-stone so that it could never be carried to war again, buried the heads, and wrote the names in the first book of the Archive in 2A 9. From that day come the Archive's rule that no elf should march until the names of the last war have been read, its keeping of every vote of the Refusal, its right to refuse any reader, king or elf, and its custom of reading the names of the fallen aloud at the road's end every spring. The unfinished book of 3A 1180 lies in the same hall as the broken spears, and the loremasters say only that both are records of something that stopped. In 4A 1748 they are copying the oldest books, and some of them have begun to ask whether a second heap of spears is coming.

sign.device: A spear broken in two, the halves laid apart with a gap between them, in quay silver on night sea: the Broken Spears of the Road's End.
sign.origin: The broken spear is the first deed of the Archive: in 2A 9 the witnesses of Lenkei broke the spears of the elves who fell in the Ember Lands across the treaty-stone at the road's end and wrote each name before they let the companies pass. The loremasters sewed one broken spear on the cloth that covers the Book of the Fallen, and they carry that cloth as a banner whenever the Archive's books leave Lenkei. The halves are always shown apart and never mended.
sign.meaning: That war is read before it is waged: to the Kindred a warning that every march is paid for in names, and to anyone who would ask the elves to fight a promise that the Archive will read him the cost first.

dynasties.name: The Archivists of Lenkei
dynasties.notable: The loremasters choose an Archivist from among themselves; the Archivist keeps the keys of the Archive and may refuse any reader, king or elf.

events.name: The Treaty of Passage
events.summary: The loremasters keep a treaty older than the Archive's first book: the road of the eastern kingdom may cross the elven shore, and no army of that kingdom may come with it.

events.name: The Book of the Fallen
events.summary: The loremasters write the first book of the Archive, the names of the elves who fell in the war against Volgan and in the Ember Lands, and lay it at the end of the old roads where every traveller must pass it.

events.name: The Spears Laid Down
events.summary: The companies home from the Ember Lands lay the spears of their fallen at the road's end, and the witnesses of Lenkei break each one across the treaty-stone and write its bearer's name before they let the living pass.

events.name: The Refusal Recorded
events.summary: The Archive writes down the votes of every realm in the Refusal and the reasons each gave, and keeps the record open for any elf who wants to argue with it.

events.name: The Unfinished Book
events.summary: A loremaster stops writing in the middle of a sentence in one of the Archive's books and never finishes it; the loremasters keep the book and will not say who stopped writing or why.

countries.capitalReason: Lenkei, the Archive, stands at the southern end of the rift coast where the old roads stop, so that every road of the Kindred ends at its door.
countries.today: Eldafaen in 4A 1748 is the House of the Archive, some 8,000 elves on the southern rift shore and Endelond, keeping the records of the Kindred and refusing readers it does not trust. It lies on the rift and so in the path of any eastern landing, and its loremasters have begun copying the oldest books in case they must carry them away.

divergence.what: The Archivist opens the Archive's oldest books to scholars of men.
divergence.consequence: What the Archive knows of the First Men becomes a matter of argument in Parim and the Lost Cause, years before anyone there is ready for it.

divergence.what: The eastern host lands on the southern shore and the loremasters carry the Archive inland.
divergence.consequence: The books survive the war in the Magical Forest's keeping, and the southern rift shore is left with empty shelves and no defenders.

divergence.what: A realm of the Kindred marches to war before the Archive has read the names of the last one.
divergence.consequence: The loremasters close the Archive to that realm, the precedent of 2A 9 is broken, and the Elder Moot must decide whether the Archive's rule binds the living.

countries.name: Yavieth

founding.story: The dragons of Dragon Mountain roosted on its three spurs before there were elves in the green strip beneath them, the roost-keepers say, and the first keepers were elves who went up to the roosts to listen rather than to command. They have lived under the mountain ever since without a ruler, keeping the roosts and the bond, and no realm of the elves commands a dragon without their word.

roots.story: The roost-keepers say the dragons roosted on the three spurs of Dragon Mountain before any elf lived in the green strip beneath them, and that the first keepers came not to tame them but to listen. Long before Aen, by their telling, a band of elves fleeing a hard winter on the Magic Mountains sheltered under the spurs, and a dragon came down among them in the night and did not harm them; in the morning it had gone and had left one shed scale, still warm, beside their fire. The eldest of the band took the scale for a word given and climbed to the roost to give it back, and the dragon would not take it; the bond began with that refused gift. From it come all the customs of Yavieth: the keepers have no ruler, only an eldest who climbs to speak; a dragon never forgets a name and never says one, so the keepers keep no lists; they take only shed scale and never draw a dragon's blood; the dragon-shy goats on the slopes are the dragons' whenever the dragons want them; and no realm of the Kindred asks a dragon for help without the keepers' word. The bond was wounded in 1A 1600, when dragons corrupted to Volgan's service took two roosts of the western spur, and the keepers still will not say how the spur was made clean. In 4A 1748 the First Scale is kept at Thoriveniel wrapped in green cloth, and to the keepers the scale trade at Kingson is the sale of what the dragons have given up, never of anything taken from them.

sign.device: A single shed dragon scale, point down, above the three spurs of Dragon Mountain, in keeper silver on slope green: the First Scale.
sign.origin: The scale is the First Scale, the one a dragon left beside the fire of the first keepers and would not take back, and the three spurs beneath it are the roosts where the bond is kept. The keepers carried it on a cloth to Kingson when the scale trade began in 4A 120, so that the market would know whose goods these were, and they hang it at the roost-mouth whenever the eldest keeper goes up to speak. The keepers never show the dragon itself, because a dragon is no one's sign.
sign.meaning: That the bond is a gift and not a bridle: to the Kindred a promise that the dragons can still be asked, and to any power that would turn or bind a dragon a warning that the keepers stand between it and the roosts.

dynasties.name: The Eldest Keepers
dynasties.notable: The fellowship has no ruler; the eldest keeper speaks to the dragons and the rest listen to the eldest. The keepers say a dragon never forgets a name and never says one, and so they keep no list of eldest keepers.

events.name: The First Scale
events.summary: Elves sheltering from a hard winter under the three spurs are spared by a dragon, which leaves a shed scale by their fire and will not take it back when their eldest climbs to return it; the keepers count the bond from that night.

events.name: The Corrupted Roosts
events.summary: Dragons corrupted to Volgan's service fly against the Grand Alliance, and the keepers lose two roosts of the western spur to the corruption; the keepers do not speak of how the spur was made clean again.

events.name: The Scale Trade
events.summary: The keepers begin to trade shed dragon-scale at Kingson's market for salt and iron, and the scale becomes the Kingson Pass's most valuable cargo.

events.name: The Long Winter
events.summary: When Kingson doubles its toll on elven goods, the keepers stop the scale trade with the Magical Forest's closing of the eastern fort, and the vale's merchants learn what a winter without dragon-scale costs.

countries.capitalReason: Thoriveniel is the keepers' shelter on the slope of Greenland under the three spurs, close enough to the roosts to hear the dragons and far enough not to be eaten by them.
countries.today: Yavieth in 4A 1748 is a fellowship of some 6,000 roost-keepers under Dragon Mountain, without a ruler, keeping the roosts and the bond between the elves and the dragons. It trades dragon-scale at Kingson and grazes dragon-shy goats, which the dragons are allowed to take, on the green slopes beneath the mountain.

divergence.what: A dragon is turned from the roosts by a dark power before the war.
divergence.consequence: The keepers lose the trust of the Kindred, the skies over the Middle Lands become dangerous to everyone, and the bond must be remade or broken.

divergence.what: The eldest keeper entrusts a dragon to a stranger the elves vouch for.
divergence.consequence: The heir returns to the Middle Lands by air with the wizard and his servant, as history has it, and the keepers become a party to a war of men.

divergence.what: The First Scale is stolen from Thoriveniel.
divergence.consequence: The eldest keeper must climb to the roosts without it, the dragons grow restless over the Magical Lands, and every realm suspects whichever realm would gain most from a dragon asked without the keepers' word.

countries.name: Teste

founding.story: In the early Third Age families fleeing the Vale crossed the Kingson Pass and came to the lakes of Andos Enda, where the lake elves sheltered them for a night and sent them on at dawn, as they send every guest. Some of them walked north to the empty Teste Vale under the Herrodon rim, the one fertile valley of the northern Magical Lands, and asked Herrodon's queen for leave to stay; she gave it in return for grain, and Teste has fed her hall since.

roots.story: The men of Teste descend from the rangers and field-folk of the Vale who fled the Necromancer's Order over the Kingson Pass in the early Third Age, carrying seed-grain sewn into their hoods because it was the one thing the Order's collectors had not found. The lake elves of Andos Enda sheltered them for a night and sent them on at dawn, as they send every guest, and the families walked north all day without knowing where they were going. At dusk Halvar, who led them, saw swallows dropping into a valley under the Herrodon rim, and he said that swallows come down only where there is water, mud for a nest and fields to hunt over; they followed the birds and found the empty Teste Vale. The grandmothers' saying that they were sent away at dawn and came home at dusk is the story of that day, and the commune keeps it by shutting its gate at dawn on the founding day and opening it at dusk. From the hood-seed come the vale's first fields and its bargain to feed Herrodon's hall; from the Vale they left come their old ranger speech, a Reeve chosen every year instead of a lord, and the limit on a Reeve's years that followed Halvar's twenty; and from the swallows comes the rule that no one in the vale pulls down a nest under an eave. In 4A 1748 the commune still sows a handful of grain of the hood-seed line first in every field, and it has not forgotten that the Vale it fled lies just over the pass.

sign.device: A swallow diving with its wings swept back, in straw on vale green: the Dusk Swallow of Testebur.
sign.origin: The swallow is the bird Halvar's families followed at dusk on the day the lake elves sent them on, down into the empty vale that became their home. The families sewed it on the cloth that covered the first seed-sack opened in the vale, that cloth hung over the first harvest moot, and every Reeve since has been chosen under a swallow banner. It is shown diving, as the birds came down to the vale, and never rising.
sign.meaning: That a people sent away can come home: to Herrodon a reminder of the grain bargain kept, and to the Vale over the pass a promise that its exiles remember the road back.

dynasties.name: The Reeves of the Vale
dynasties.notable: The commune chooses a Reeve every year at the harvest moot; a Reeve may be chosen again, but none has been chosen more than five years running since the first, Halvar, who held it for twenty.

events.name: Sent On at Dawn
events.summary: The families leave the lake groves at dawn and settle the Teste Vale under Herrodon's protection; the vale's grandmothers say they were sent away at dawn and came home at dusk.

events.name: The Swallows at Dusk
events.summary: At the end of their first day's walk from the lakes Halvar sees swallows dropping into a valley under the Herrodon rim, and the families follow the birds down into the empty Teste Vale.

events.name: The Hungry Year
events.summary: When the Black Roots blight the Magical Lands' fields, Teste's grain feeds Herrodon and Andos Enda both, and the lake elves send the commune a boat every spring in thanks.

events.name: The Deliverer's Chapel
events.summary: Pilgrims from the Zilin Hills build the vale's first chapel of the Deliverer beside the old hearth-shrine of the twelve, and the commune keeps both.

countries.capitalReason: Testebur stands where the Teste Brook leaves the vale, at the only road out, so that the commune's market can sell its grain to Herrodon's hall and the lake boats without letting either into the fields.
countries.today: Teste in 4A 1748 is a valley commune of some 55,000 men under a Reeve chosen at the harvest moot, under Herrodon's protection, speaking an old ranger dialect of Aenoran. It feeds Herrodon and Andos Enda with grain and is the only land of men in the northern Magical Lands.

divergence.what: In the war the commune sends its grain west over the Kingson Pass to the Vale it fled.
divergence.consequence: Herrodon's hall goes short, the queen's protection is tested, and the families of Teste meet the descendants of those who stayed behind.

divergence.what: The living stones of the Lustras Hills come down onto the Teste road in a hard year.
divergence.consequence: The commune must ask Herrodon for help it has never needed, and the queen must decide what the bargain of 3A 150 obliges her to do.

divergence.what: In a year of war the commune keeps its gate shut past dusk on the founding day and turns refugees away.
divergence.consequence: Teste breaks its own oldest custom to protect its fields, Herrodon's queen asks whether a people sent on at dawn may send others on, and the vale's families divide over it.

countries.name: Luv-zhise

founding.story: Alerhic boatmen from the eastern shore had run ferries across the Rift Narrows for centuries without leave from anyone, and when the Order fell they asked the elder houses of the rift coast for a charter. The elves granted the quay-houses a strip of the Mushroom coast at the narrowest crossing under the quay-book's law, and the free port of Luv-zhise has lived on the crossing to the East ever since, men, elves and mycid traders together.

roots.story: The quay-folk of Luv-zhise are Alerhic boat-families whose oldest songs say they were the people of the city that stood astride the neck of land before it broke. When the sea came in long before Aen, the city broke with the land; its western half lies under the fungal belt of the shore beside the port, and its eastern half under the grass of the Delbiz coast. The boat-families stayed on the water between the halves and began ferrying travellers over the place where the road had run, steering by the tops of drowned pillars and causeway footings that still show at low water, and the ferries have run ever since without a break that anyone remembers. From that loss comes the port's whole character: the river families and the temple families who share the office of Quay-Master, the Lake Litany of the River Temples kept beside the twelve, the pillar-marks every pilot must learn before he may take a ferry across, a habit of siding with whoever holds the crossing, and an old hope among the temple families that the two halves of the city will one day stand on one shore again. Blosian Furanides won the charter of 4A 140 from the elves by ferrying the quay-book's keepers across in a storm without charging a fare, and every Quay-Master since crosses once a year without a fare in his memory. In 4A 1748 the quay-houses still swear in each new Quay-Master under the half arch of the Western Gate, the last standing piece of the old city, which rises out of the water at the port's edge.

sign.device: A half arch broken at its crown, rising from a single pier, in quay ochre on narrows teal: the Western Gate.
sign.origin: The half arch is the Western Gate, the last standing piece of the city that crossed the neck before the land broke; it rises from the water at the port's edge and can be seen from the Delbiz shore on a clear day. The ferrymen steered by it before there was a port, painted it on their prows as the mark of the crossing, and sewed it on the quay-houses' banner when the elves granted the charter of 4A 140. It is shown broken at the crown because the other half stands on the far shore.
sign.meaning: That the crossing is kept: to travellers a promise that the ferries run in any weather, to the far shore an old kinship and an old quarrel, and to an invader a warning that the quay-folk can sink the ferries and leave the gate standing alone again.

dynasties.name: The Quay-Houses of Hisemrak
dynasties.notable: The heads of the quay-houses sit as the port's council and choose a Quay-Master each year; the river families with names in -ides and the temple families with names in -os have shared the office for six centuries. Blosian Furanides won the charter and was the first Quay-Master.

events.name: Ferries over the Drowned Road
events.summary: After the neck breaks, the quay folk ferry travellers over the water where the road ran, past pillars and causeway footings that lie under the fungal belt of the shore.

events.name: The Charter of the Narrows
events.summary: The rift-coast elves grant the Alerhic quay-houses their charter, and Luv-zhise becomes a free port under the quay-book.

events.name: The Oath Under the Gate
events.summary: The quay-houses swear in their first Quay-Master under the half arch of the Western Gate, and the crossing without a fare that Blosian made in the storm becomes the yearly duty of every Quay-Master after him.

events.name: The Mycid Market
events.summary: Mycid traders from the Mushroom Forest begin to come to the port's market with fungi, dyes and spore-cloth, and the port learns to trade with people whose speech no one has ever written down.

events.name: The Spore Summer
events.summary: A summer of heavy spore-air closes the Rift Road through the fungal belt for a season and the port's ferries carry everything; the quay-houses double their fares and the Elder of Lccimio halves them again.

rivalries.nature: The ferry trade runs to the Delbiz coast across the Narrows, and the two shores have argued over fares, wrecks and runaway sailors for six centuries.

countries.capitalReason: Hisemrak, the old quay town, stands on the Mushroom coast at the Rift Narrows, the shortest crossing to the East, where the first ferrymen tied up their boats before anyone gave them leave.
countries.today: Luv-zhise in 4A 1748 is a free port of some 80,000, Alerhic quay-folk with rift-coast elves and mycid traders among them, ruled by its quay-houses under the elves' charter. It lives on the crossing to the East, keeps the River Temples' Lake Litany beside the twelve, and will side with whoever holds the rift crossing.

divergence.what: When the eastern host comes to the Narrows, the quay-houses sink their ferries.
divergence.consequence: The host must cross the rift elsewhere and later, the port loses its living, and the Magical Lands gain a season.

divergence.what: The quay-houses carry the eastern host across for gold.
divergence.consequence: The Narrows open on the first day of the invasion, the rift coast falls before the Kindred can gather, and the port becomes the host's harbour.

divergence.what: The temple families persuade an eastern crown to raise the far half of the gate again on the Delbiz shore.
divergence.consequence: The quay-folk claim both shores of the crossing, Delbiz and the rift-coast elves both object, and the Narrows become a prize instead of a passage.

countries.name: Mushroom Forest

founding.story: The belt of giant fungi along the rift shore has been the mycids' land for as long as the rift-coast elves remember, and the elves have never tried to rule it. Nobody outside the forest knows how the mycids came there, how they decide anything or what they call themselves; the traders of Luv-zhise know only that the mycids come to the forest's edge to trade and that strangers find the spore-air hard to breathe in summer.

roots.story: What is known of the mycids' past is only what other peoples have seen of them, and the rift-coast elves, who have watched the belt longest, insist that it is very little. Their oldest rolls say the belt of giant fungi already stood on the rift shore when the neck of land broke long before Aen, and that it grew over the western half of the drowned city on that shore, so that pillars and causeway footings now stand among the stems; the quay-folk of Luv-zhise steer by the ones that reach the water. The elves have never ruled the belt and say they have never been asked in. The one great deed anyone can tell of the belt came in the Third Age: when the Black Roots crept through the land's magic toward the rift coast in 3A 820, the fungi grew over them and the dead roots rotted away there, while the elves of the north had to fell their own wood to stop them. Whether the mycids did this, allowed it or only lived through it, nobody outside the forest knows, and the mycids have never said. Since 4A 388 they have come to the market of Luv-zhise in rings, standing in a circle, with fungi, dyes and spore-cloth, and every bale they bring bears the same stamped mark: a pale cap rising from a black severed root. The traders read the mark as the belt's own memory of the Black Roots; the mycids have never explained it, and the quay-books record it as the only sign of the mycids that anyone has.

sign.device: A pale cap rising from a black severed root, in cap cream and loam dark on spore purple: the Bale-Mark of the rings.
sign.origin: The cap on the severed root is the mark stamped on every bale the mycids have brought to the market of Luv-zhise since 4A 388, and it is the only sign of theirs that any other people has seen. The quay-houses copied it onto the cloth that marks the mycids' place at the market, and the rift-coast elves read it as the belt remembering the Black Roots it rotted away in 3A 820. What the mycids themselves mean by it has never been said.
sign.meaning: Read by others as a warning that what is dead in the belt feeds what grows there, and as a sign that the belt cannot be poisoned; what it means to the mycids is not known.

dynasties.name: The Rings at the Forest Edge
dynasties.notable: The quay-books of Luv-zhise call the gatherings of mycids that meet traders at the forest's edge rings, because they stand in a circle; whether a ring is a ruler, a family or only a market is not known to anyone outside the forest.

events.name: The Dead Roots Stopped
events.summary: When the Black Roots reach the rift coast, the fungi of the belt grow over them and the dead roots rot; the rift-coast elves say so, and the mycids have never said anything about it.

events.name: The First Mycid Market
events.summary: Mycid traders come to the market of Luv-zhise with fungi, dyes and spore-cloth, and the quay-books record trade with them for the first time.

events.name: The Bale-Mark
events.summary: In the second season of the mycid market the quay-books first describe the mark on the mycids' bales, a pale cap rising from a black severed root, and copy it onto the cloth that marks their place.

events.name: The Spore Summer
events.summary: A summer of heavy spore-air closes the Rift Road through the belt for a season; nobody who tried to cross it came out sooner than a month later.

countries.capitalReason: No seat of the mycids is recorded, and no trader has been taken to one; the forest's heart, which the traders never see, is held to be where the mycids live because it is where they go when they leave the market.
countries.today: The Mushroom Forest in 4A 1748 is the land of some 12,000 mycids along the rift shore, an isolated community that trades through Luv-zhise and keeps its own counsel. It lies on the rift coast and so among the first lands in the path of anyone who crosses from the East.

divergence.what: A realm of the Kindred asks the mycids for passage through the belt in the war, and they grant it.
divergence.consequence: The Rift Road opens to an elven host or to refugees, and the mycids are drawn into a war of other peoples.

divergence.what: The eastern host lands on the fungal coast and burns its way inland.
divergence.consequence: The mycids are scattered, the spore-air turns on the host as it turns on every stranger, and the quay-books of Luv-zhise record the mycids' market ending.

countries.name: Worshipdom

founding.story: A hermit of the Deliverer built a hermitage in the central of the three Zilin valleys south of the Magical Forest, among the healing herbs the elves had never cut, and pilgrims began to come to it from the Middle Lands over the South Pass. Within a few years the hermitage was a house, the house a town, and the valleys a small temple-state with almost no army, whose strength is its pilgrims, its couriers and its confessors.

roots.story: Long before Aen an old road of the East came through the Zilin Hills on its way west to the South Pass, and its travellers rested in the three valleys at stone wells and hostels whose foundations still lie under the herb-meadows. The road died when the land to the east broke, the hostels fell in, and for ages the valleys belonged only to the healing herbs, which the elves of the Magical Forest would not cut and would let no one else cut. A hermit of the Deliverer came there in 4A 1520 because, the pilgrims say, the old wells still ran, and in the famine winter of the hermitage's third year he baked bread for every traveller who came over the South Pass from the hermitage's one oven, giving away the loaf before he asked the stranger's name. From that winter comes the valleys' first rule, that a pilgrim house feeds and doctors a guest before it asks who he is, and the Worshipdom's whole public character grew from it: the hostels on the old road, the herb-physicians, the famine stores, the couriers who carry any court's letters for a small fee, and the elves' condition of 4A 1524 that no pilgrim cuts a living tree, which the houses keep strictly. The hermit's oven still stands in Lenlakron and is lit on feast days to bake the loaves given to the first pilgrims of the season, and the valleys have never raised more than their hill wardens. In 4A 1748 the Worshipdom's houses stand on the caravan roads, in Parim and across the sea, and every one of them keeps a bread-shelf by its door.

sign.device: A hand reaching up from the base and offering a round loaf, in bread brown on hostel white: the Hermit's Loaf.
sign.origin: The hand and loaf are the Hermit's Loaf, the bread the first hermit of the valleys gave to every traveller over the South Pass in the famine winter of the hermitage's third year, before he asked the stranger's name. The pilgrims who carried word of it back to the lake towns sewed a hand and a loaf on the pennons of their staves, and the first High Confessor took it as the valleys' arms when the houses of the Magical Forest granted the three valleys in 4A 1524. Every pilgrim house of the Worshipdom shows it over its door.
sign.meaning: That a guest is fed before he is questioned: to pilgrims, the poor and the courts a promise of charity and welcome, and to the valleys' neighbours an assurance that the Worshipdom is a house of alms and not of arms.

dynasties.name: The High Confessors of Lenlakron
dynasties.notable: The temple-state is led by a High Confessor chosen by the abbots of the pilgrim houses, with an Abbot-Steward who runs the valleys; Ilvane is High Confessor in 4A 1748 and Lozan Heron Abbot-Steward.

events.name: The Wells of the Old Road
events.summary: An old road of the East passes through the Zilin Hills toward the South Pass, and its travellers rest at stone wells and hostels in the three valleys whose foundations still lie under the herb-meadows.

events.name: The Hermitage
events.summary: A hermitage of the Deliverer is built among the herbs of the central Zilin valley, and the first pilgrims come to it from the lake towns.

events.name: The Famine Winter
events.summary: In a winter of hunger the hermit bakes bread for every traveller over the South Pass from the hermitage's one oven and gives each loaf before he asks the stranger's name, and the valleys' first rule is made.

events.name: The Valleys Granted
events.summary: The Magical Forest's houses grant the three valleys to the hermitage as pilgrim ground on condition that no pilgrim cuts a living tree, and the first High Confessor is chosen.

events.name: The Pilgrim Road
events.summary: The pilgrim road over the South Pass is opened under escort of the Klungori Guard and the Nolorim wardens, and the Worshipdom pays both their fees without complaint.

events.name: The Courier Rule
events.summary: The pilgrim houses begin carrying letters for any court that asks, at a small fee, and within a generation the Worshipdom's couriers are welcome in every capital of Aoaz.

events.name: The Blessing of the League
events.summary: The High Confessor blesses the Lost Cause at its founding, and the Golden King gives the valleys a gilded reliquary that the pilgrims are shown on feast days.

countries.capitalReason: Lenlakron grew round the hermitage in the central of the three Zilin valleys, where the herbs grow thickest and the pilgrim road from the South Pass comes down; every pilgrim house in the valleys is a day's walk from it.
countries.today: The Worshipdom in 4A 1748 is a gentle temple-state of some 150,000 pilgrim-folk in the three Zilin valleys under High Confessor Ilvane, holding little land and almost no army. Its hostels shelter pilgrims of the Deliverer from every land, its couriers carry letters for every court, and its confessors are welcome in Parim, the East and the North alike.

divergence.what: A neighbour annexes the Zilin valleys before the year of the King's death.
divergence.consequence: The pilgrim roads close, the temples of Aenor lose their most honoured voice, and the crown's succession must be settled without the valleys' blessing.

divergence.what: When the temples of Parim proclaim the Deliverer king, the High Confessor waits before giving the valleys' blessing.
divergence.consequence: The Faithful hold Parim without the Worshipdom's voice, the Thirty Days run long, and the other camps gain time.

divergence.what: In a hard famine the pilgrim houses begin to ask a guest's name before they feed him.
divergence.consequence: The pilgrims' trust in the valleys wavers, the couriers find hungry courts less welcoming, and the Worshipdom's charity becomes a question in Parim.

cities.name: Lyrion
cities.legend: The tree-city grew round the oldest Singing Grove, and the council elves say the grove still sings when the houses vote unanimously, which is why it is so seldom heard.
cities.economy: The council of houses, the book of precedents, the Elder Moot; fallen timber, healing herbs and silver from the Magic Mountains.

cities.name: Verozo
cities.legend: The queen's hall keeps an empty seat for the Eldest of the lost household of the west, and the hall-keepers dust it every morning so that it will be ready if she ever comes.
cities.economy: The hill queen's hall, grain from Teste, the hard ore of the rim, hill herds.

cities.name: Enliras
cities.legend: The water-garden of the Water-Court floats half on the largest lake, and the lake elves say that a judgement given there is carried by the water to every grove before the judge has finished speaking.
cities.economy: The Water-Court, lake fishing, boats, the letters to Sonargur.

cities.name: Boundary Groves
cities.legend: Both realms tend the groves on the Andos Water, and the lake elves say the trees lean toward Herrodon in the morning and toward Enliras in the evening, so that neither side can claim them by noon.
cities.economy: None; rites, embassies and the oldest feud of the Kindred.

cities.name: Ennaton
cities.legend: The wardens' hall on the West Pass keeps the watch-fire lit since the Oath of the Posts, and the wardens say the fire has gone out only once, and the warden on duty that night is still apologising.
cities.economy: The wardenship's hall, pass tolls and the count of pilgrims, hill goats.

cities.name: Hidirim
cities.legend: The quay-book is kept in a chest on the harbour wall, and the shore's sailors say an eastern captain who lies to the harbour-master will find his ship's name already written in it, under the wrong cargo.
cities.economy: Quays, orchards, fruit and wine, the eastern trade across the rift.

cities.name: Lenkei
cities.legend: At the Archive where the old roads stop, the loremasters keep a book that ends in the middle of a sentence and will not say who stopped writing; travellers who ask are shown the book and not the page.
cities.economy: The Archive's copyists and readers, the rift fishery, gifts of every elven realm.

cities.name: Thoriveniel
cities.legend: The keepers' shelter under the three spurs is roofed with shed dragon-scale, and the keepers say a dragon flying over it knows it is welcome by the colour the roof shines back.
cities.economy: Dragon-scale traded at Kingson, dragon-shy goats, the roosts.

cities.name: Testebur
cities.legend: The vale's grandmothers say their grandmothers' grandmothers were sent away from the lakes at dawn and came home to Testebur at dusk, and the town still shuts its gate at dawn and opens it at dusk on the founding day.
cities.economy: Grain for Herrodon and Andos Enda, the harvest moot, the vale's two chapels.

cities.name: Hisemrak
cities.legend: The first ferrymen tied up their boats at Hisemrak before anyone gave them leave, and the quay-houses still pay the rift-coast elves one rope a year for the right to have done it.
cities.economy: The ferries across the Rift Narrows, the mycid market, fungi, dyes and spore-cloth, tolls.

cities.name: Lenlakron
cities.legend: The pilgrims say the herbs round the first hermitage grew greener in the year it was built, and every pilgrim takes a leaf home pressed in a book of hours.
cities.economy: Pilgrim hostels, healing herbs, the couriers' fees, alms.

figures.name: Halvar of Teste
figures.role: First Reeve of the Teste Vale
figures.biography: One of the refugees the lake elves sent on at dawn, Halvar led the families north to the empty vale under the Herrodon rim, struck the grain bargain with the queen of Herrodon and was Reeve for twenty years; every Reeve since has been forbidden to hold the office as long.

figures.name: Blosian Furanides
figures.biography: An Alerhic ferry-master of the river families, Blosian asked the elder houses of the rift coast for the charter of the Narrows in 4A 140 and won it by bringing the quay-book's keepers across the rift in his own boat, in a storm, without charging a fare.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The book of precedents
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The council elves decide by the precedents of their book, and every vote, including the Refusal of 2A 2121, becomes a page that a later vote must answer.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Refusal
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Elves help elves, not the crowns of men: no elven realm sends an army at a human king's request, though healers and travellers may go where they like.

lawsAndCustoms.name: Sent on at dawn
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The lake elves shelter every guest for one night and send him on at dawn; the men of Teste keep the founding day by shutting their gate at dawn and opening it at dusk.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The quay-book
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The law of ships, tolls and quarantine of the rift coast since 2A 300: a ship turned away from one harbour may not be taken in at the next.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Oath of the Posts
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Each warden family keeps one post on the heights, and a Pass-Warden on whose watch a vigil is broken is unmade.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The roost-keepers' word
lawsAndCustoms.summary: No realm of the Kindred asks a dragon for help without the roost-keepers' word, and the keepers give it only when the eldest keeper has spoken to the dragon.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The Speaking Bough
lawsAndCustoms.summary: A house speaks in the council only while it holds a bough the grove has let fall, and no house breaks a bough from a living tree; the First Speaker takes office by picking the bough up from the floor.

lawsAndCustoms.name: No one left in the snow
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Since the White Winter the queen of Herrodon is bound to send out for anyone of the hills who is lost, and her hall keeps a seat empty for the household that never came home.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The court afloat
lawsAndCustoms.summary: The Water-Court sits in a boat on open water so that no grove owns its ground, and the Speaker owns no land while in office.

lawsAndCustoms.name: Names before spears
lawsAndCustoms.summary: No elf should march until the Archive has read the names of the fallen of the last war; the loremasters read them at the road's end every spring.

lawsAndCustoms.name: The fare not taken
lawsAndCustoms.summary: Every Quay-Master crosses the Rift Narrows once a year without charging a fare, in memory of Blosian's crossing in the storm of 4A 140.
